description: Two-stage variant of Linha Fina: intents are partitioned by skill_id, a top-level classifier maps the query to a single skill_id first, and only that skill's per-intent SVM engine resolves the intent. Same distribution and confidence gate as linha-fina-medium, registered under a separate opm.pipeline entry point (HierarchicalLinhaFinaPipeline in linha_fina/hierarchical_opm.py). Needs at least 2 domains and 3 intents globally before either stage can train (the plugin's own constraint).
notes: Same medium-confidence gate and thresholds as linha-fina-medium; 'domain_threshold': 0.0 keeps the top-level domain gate disabled (shipped default) so the comparison isolates the two-stage routing shape from linha-fina-domain-medium's parallel-argmax shape. Hypothesis: domain-first gating should help precision on large multi-domain sets by rejecting cross-domain queries before any sub-engine scores, and be weaker or equal on small single-domain sets where the domain classifier has too little signal to train reliably. KNOWN BROKEN as of linha-fina 0.3.0a1: LinhaFinaPipeline.handle_initial_train (linha_fina/opm.py:138) calls self.containers[lang].train(), but HierarchicalLinhaFinaPipeline's containers are HierarchicalIntentEngine instances which have no .train() method (AttributeError on 'mycroft.ready') -- confirmed by a live train/match sanity run in this PR. Needs an upstream fix in linha-fina before this fighter can produce real predictions; kept in the registry so a fix is picked up automatically.
